messages.text: Alcaraz felt burnt out after too much exposure on and off the court

metadata.summary: Carlos Alcaraz has admitted feeling burnt out due to being exposed to a lot of commitments before he suffered a lengthy layoff due to an injury sustained in April.
metadata.content: Laver Cup: Carlos Alcaraz felt burnt out due to exposure before a lengthy layoff with a wrist injury | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Laver Cup: Carlos Alcaraz felt burnt out due to exposure before a lengthy layoff with a wrist injury Carlos Alcaraz reveals he "wants to miss tennis sometimes" after feeling burnt out from all his commitments before his injury lay-off; you can watch the Laver Cup at The O2 in London from 25-27 September live on Sky Sports Thursday 24 September 2026 12:13, UK Image: Carlos Alcaraz felt physically and mentally exhausted before he suffered a wrist injury Carlos Alcaraz has admitted feeling burnt out due to being exposed to a lot of commitments before he suffered a lengthy layoff due to an injury sustained in April. The Spaniard, who won the Australian Open title at the start of the year, was forced to miss more than four months from tennis because of a right wrist injury . Alcaraz returned at the US Open where he reached the quarter-finals before losing a five-set thriller to American Ben Shelton , which finished at 3.33am local time. messages.text: Warwickshire close in on County Championship title after skittling Leicestershire

metadata.summary: Warwickshire took a big step towards clinching the Rothesay County Championship title after skittling relegation-threatened Leicestershire for 125 at Edgbaston.
metadata.content: County Championship: Warwickshire close in on title after skittling relegation-threatened Leicestershire | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content County Championship: Warwickshire close in on title after skittling relegation-threatened Leicestershire Thursday's County Championship sees Warwickshire move closer to title after bowling out relegation-threatened Leicestershire for 125 at Edgbaston; Warwickshire win would guarantee a first title since the Covid-shortened 2021 campaign, with second-placed Somerset struggling against Surrey Thursday 24 September 2026 20:02, UK Image: Ethan Bamber stars as Warwickshire bowl out Leicestershire for 125 to move closer to County Championship title Warwickshire took a big step towards clinching the Rothesay County Championship title after skittling relegation-threatened Leicestershire for 125 at Edgbaston. Ahead of the first day's play, Leicestershire announced plans to appeal their 27-point deduction for a substandard pitch at Grace Road in last month's win over Glamorgan - a decision that means their Division One fate could remain up in the air until the final round of fixtures this week. Only two of their batters passed 12 in Birmingham, with in-form Ethan Bamber taking 4-42 and former England seamer Chris Woakes claiming 3-20 for the Bears, who closed on 130-4 to lead by five. messages.text: Premier League in joint call for FIFA reform amid Infantino crisis

metadata.summary: The Premier League and three of its top European counterparts will on Friday issue a joint call for urgent governance reform at FIFA amid the crisis engulfing its president, Gianni Infantino.
metadata.content: Gianni Infantino: Premier League and three other top European leagues to demand FIFA reform | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Gianni Infantino: Premier League and three other top European leagues to demand FIFA reform English football's top flight and its counterparts in Germany, Italy and Spain will demand urgent reform of the game's global governance in a joint statement on Friday, Sky News understands; the joint call comes amid the crisis engulfing its FIFA president Gianni Infantino By Sky News' Mark Kleinman & Rob Harris Thursday 24 September 2026 18:53, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol explains why the Premier League have joined three of its other top European counterparts in demanding a FIFA reform against Gianni Infantino The Premier League and three of its top European counterparts will on Friday issue a joint call for urgent governance reform at FIFA amid the crisis engulfing its president, Gianni Infantino. Sky News can reveal that English football's top flight and the top domestic leagues in Germany, Italy and Spain will publish a collective statement demanding greater consultation on key issues such as the global football calendar. The statement was still in the process of being formally agreed between the quartet of domestic leagues on Thursday afternoon and it was unclear whether it would specifically call for Infantino to stand down.
